title: On‑Prem Cross‑Connect Playbook and Terraform Prototypes
body:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for engineering + field ops to onboard customer colo cross‑connects and to iterate Terraform module prototypes for on‑prem connectivity. The doc focuses on common reference patterns (single‑site colo, multi‑site EVPN, cloud breakout), recommended TF module boundaries, validation checks, and an upgrade/rollback runbook for network changes.

Scope/assumptions:
- Customer runs Redwood Private control plane in their VPC or on‑prem env.
- Connectivity options supported: direct fiber cross‑connect at colo, carrier MPLS/EVPN, cloud Interconnect/Direct Connect.
- We assume customer allows BGP peering and shared key material exchange.
- This is not a deep security design doc; use security/compliance checklists separately.

High‑level reference architectures (quick patterns):
1) Small customer — single colo cage, NAT egress
   - Single L2 cross‑connect to provider PoP, upstream router with BGP session to customer edge (CE).
   - Redwood host nodes in customer VLAN/private segment.
   - Egress via customer firewall/NAT; optional egress IP translation maintained by customer.
   - Minimal ACLs; keep control plane endpoints reachable only from management CIDR.

2) Enterprise — multi‑rack / EVPN fabric + public cloud breakout
   - EVPN fabric in colo with per‑tenant VRF.
   - BGP L3VPN between customer edge and customer cloud region (or cloud interconnect).
   - Redundant cross‑connects (A/B PoP) with active/standby BGP session preferences.
   - Route filtering: accept only specific prefixes used by Redwood.

3) Hybrid private (on‑prem + cloud dedicated)
   - Customer uses an on‑prem gateway + cloud interconnect for backup routing.
   - Smart routing at edge: prefer local egress for low latency, failover to cloud region if colo capacity constrained.

Pre‑onboarding checklist (field checklist for SE):
- Customer contact + on‑site engineer identified (name + phone).
- Physical cross‑connect scheduled with colo (LOA) and fiber pair ID.
- VLAN and tag numbers for Fordwarding/management channels assigned.
- IP addressing plan: management, compute, storage, monitoring subnets.
- BGP ASNs (customer ASN + redwood ASN) and peering IPs agreed.
- Expected RTT targets and bandwidth reservations (if applicable).
- KMS/HSM endpoints for key exchange if customer requires.
- Escalation contact list (colocation NOC, customer network ops, Redwood infra oncall).

Terraform module notes & conventions (prototypes and naming):
- Goal: provide small, composable modules per responsibility: crossconnect, bgp_peer, vlan, edge_firewall_rule, ip_plan. Keep provider‑specific details behind a thin provider adapter.
- Recommended module boundaries:
  - module/customer_edge (abstract CE: accepts provider adapter, bgp config, vlans)
  - module/crossconnect (LOA info, port id, vlan assignment)
  - module/bgp_session (local_asn, remote_asn, peer_ip_local, peer_ip_remote, auth_key)
  - module/ip_alloc (CIDR blocks, assignment map, outputs for hosts)
  - module/tfstate-lock (configure remote state + locking backend for the customer workspace)

Terraform prototype example (pseudo‑HCL):
```hcl
module "customer_crossconnect" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood/private-modules.git//crossconnect?ref=prototype-2025-09"

  colo_facility = var.colo_facility
  port_id       = var.port_id
  vlan_id       = var.management_vlan
  contact       = var.colo_contact
}

module "customer_bgp" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood/private-modules.git//bgp_peer?ref=prototype-2025-09"

  local_asn      = var.redwood_asn
  remote_asn     = var.customer_asn
  local_ip       = var.redwood_peer_ip
  remote_ip      = var.customer_peer_ip
  auth_key       = var.md5_key # optional
  advertise_cidrs = var.advertise_cidrs
}
```
Notes on TF practices:
- Keep sensitive values out of VCS. Use SOPS or the customer KMS to encrypt variable files.
- Use workspace per customer (terraform cloud or state per customer) to reduce blast radius.
- Include automated plan pipelines in CI (./scripts/ci-apply.sh) with mandatory human approval for apply.
- Add a return object on modules with: management_ips, bgp_session_id, vlan_ids. This makes downstream wiring simpler.

Validation & post‑apply checks (automated + manual):
- Terraform plan must be clean (no unexpected deletes).
- Confirm physical port shows Up in colo portal (or via provider API).
- Validate BGP adjacency: show ip bgp summary / show bgp neighbor (customer and redwood edge). Check prefixes learned.
- Ping healthcheck endpoints across the peering (three workstations across different subnets).
- Validate route filters / prefix lists applied as expected.
- End‑to‑end smoke test: deploy a minimal Redwood Private control plane node and confirm registration to control plane and model fetch.

Common pitfalls we've hit (field notes):
- VLAN mismatch between colo ticket and TF variables — always validate the VLAN tag on both sides before cutover.
- BGP MD5 misconfiguration — include MD5 test vectors in lab.
- Asymmetric routing when customer egresses model traffic — require explicit route advertising to avoid packets sent out a different link.
- TF state conflicts when two engineers apply same workspace without locking.

Upgrade & rollback runbook (network changes that affect live workloads):
1) Pre‑upgrade (2–4 days before):
   - Run compatibility matrix: ensure new kernel/agent/network config supported in current Redwood Runtime (check version matrix).
   - Add canary traffic plan & eval prompts.
   - Notify customer NOC + schedule maintenance window (include window length and rollback window).
   - Take snapshot of TF state and backup any configuration on hardware (router config).

2) Staged rollout (maintenance window):
   - Apply TF changes to a staging workspace representing the same topology first.
   - Verify BGP adjacency and controlled prefix advertisement.
   - Apply to non‑critical rack / non‑production VLAN first; run smoke tests.
   - If stable for X minutes (configurable), proceed to remaining racks.

3) Live rollback criteria and steps:
   - Hard failure triggers: loss of control plane connectivity to >5% of nodes, sustained latency > 2x SLO for >15 minutes, or severe prefix leakage.
   - Rollback path: run terraform apply using the saved pre‑upgrade state file (or use `terraform state push` to revert). For hardware changes, restore router config from saved backup.
   - Post rollback: clear route flaps, increment incident ticket notes, and schedule a root cause follow up.

Operational run commands and quick checks (example):
- BGP summary: `vtysh -c "show bgp summary"` or `show ip bgp summary` depending on platform.
- Confirm port link: `equinix metal ports get --id <port>` (or colo portal).
- Terraform plan: `TF_IN_AUTOMATION=1 terraform plan -var-file=secrets.tfvars`

Security/compliance reminders:
- Do not commit community keys. Exchange keys over SOPS‑encrypted artifact or customer KMS.
- ACLs for management plane must allow only specific IPs and rekeying should be scheduled quarterly (or per customer policy).
- Ensure audit logging (syslog, netflow) streams to customer SIEM or Redwood observability per contract.

Field tips (short):
- Ask colo NOC for real port signal test (simple pings across the fiber endpoint) before scheduling BGP.
- Have a spare jump host in both colo racks for last‑mile troubleshooting.
- Expect 30–60 minute unpredictability window during initial BGP convergence on first cutover.

Next steps / TODOs in this doc (working list):
- [ ] Finalize module input schema for `bgp_peer` (Maya)
- [ ] Produce small lab guide for MD5 and password‑protected BGP sessions (Tomás)
- [ ] Add TF CI job templates for customer workspaces (Lina)
- [ ] Run canary on internal staging colo by end of Q4 2025 (owner: Ravi)

Appendix — quick TF variable suggestion (example values):
```
variable "colo_facility" { default = "nyc1" }
variable "port_id" { default = "eqx-abc-123" }
variable "management_vlan" { default = 410 }
variable "redwood_asn" { default = 64512 }
variable "customer_asn" { default = 65123 }
variable "redwood_peer_ip" { default = "10.200.0.1/30" }
variable "customer_peer_ip" { default = "10.200.0.2/30" }
```
If anything in this playbook conflicts with existing customer contracts or colo restrictions, escalate to eng‑private‑deployments channel immediately. This doc will be iterated; keep notes inline and mark changes with initials.
